goals.title: Coordinate-Plane Graphs
goals.description: Use ordered pairs, axes, scales, and intercepts to read and create graphs.
i_can_statements: Plot and read ordered pairs.
Use the x- and y-axes correctly.
Read a graph using its scale.
Identify and interpret intercepts when they are shown.

goals.title: Slope in Four Views
goals.description: Find slope or rate of change from a graph, table, equation, or context.
i_can_statements: Find slope from a graph.
Find slope from a table.
Find slope from an equation.
Find and interpret rate of change from a context.

goals.title: Evaluate Expressions
goals.description: Evaluate numerical and algebraic expressions using substitution and order of operations.
i_can_statements: Substitute a value for a variable.
Use order of operations correctly.
Evaluate expressions with positive and negative numbers.
Check whether an answer is reasonable.

goals.title: Input / Output Rules
goals.description: Use an input-output rule to find values, ordered pairs, and patterns.
i_can_statements: Use input/output language and ordered pairs.
Use a rule to find an output from an input.
Find a missing input or output when enough information is given.
Use a rule to build or extend a table.

goals.title: Compare Relationships
goals.description: Compare relationships across graphs, tables, equations, and contexts using clear evidence.
i_can_statements: Compare two relationships shown in different representations.
Use values, rates, starting values, or patterns as evidence.
Explain which relationship is greater, faster, or starts higher when the question asks.
Support a comparison with information from the representations.

goals.title: One-Step Inequalities
goals.description: Solve one-step inequalities and show the solution on a number line.
i_can_statements: Solve a one-step inequality.
Reverse the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.
Use an open or closed circle correctly.
Shade the correct direction on a number line.

goals.title: Function or Not a Function
goals.description: Use inputs and outputs to decide whether a relationship is a function.
i_can_statements: Decide whether a table is a function.
Decide whether ordered pairs or a mapping are a function.
Use a graph to decide whether each input has only one output.
Explain why a relationship is or is not a function.

goals.title: Move Between Representations
goals.description: Create a new representation of a relationship and check that the important values and pattern stay the same.
i_can_statements: Make a graph from a table.
Make a table from a rule or equation.
Use a context to make a table, graph, or rule when enough information is given.
Check matching inputs, outputs, and patterns to make sure the representations agree.

goals.title: Connect Representations
goals.description: Connect tables, graphs, equations/rules, function notation, and contexts for the same relationship.
i_can_statements: Use input/output language and ordered pairs.
Evaluate a function for a given input and interpret the output.
Move among tables, graphs, equations/rules, f(x) notation, and contexts.
Use values, rates, patterns, and features as evidence.

goals.title: Understand Functions and Families
goals.description: Use function notation and key features to describe functions and recognize common function families.
i_can_statements: Use function notation such as f(x) to name and evaluate outputs.
Use the function idea already learned: each input has only one output.
Recognize basic linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute-value patterns.
Use a graph, table, equation, or context as evidence.

goals.title: Equivalent Expressions
goals.description: Use structure, like terms, the distributive property, and substitution to make equivalent expressions.
i_can_statements: Identify terms, coefficients, and factors.
Combine like terms.
Use the distributive property correctly.
Check whether two expressions are equivalent.

goals.title: Equations in Context
goals.description: Write an equation from a situation, solve when needed, and explain what the solution means.
i_can_statements: Define a variable for a situation.
Write an equation that matches the situation.
Use equivalent steps to solve when needed.
Check and interpret the solution in context.

goals.title: Slope and Rate of Change
goals.description: Find slope across representations and explain what it means.
i_can_statements: Find slope from a graph, table, equation, or two points.
Use rise/run consistently.
Interpret slope with units in a context.
Recognize positive, negative, zero, and undefined slope.

goals.title: Graph and Write Linear Functions
goals.description: Use slope and starting value to graph and write linear functions.
i_can_statements: Graph a line from slope and an intercept.
Write a linear equation from a graph, table, or context.
Use f(x) notation to evaluate a linear function.
Identify meaningful domain and range from a linear graph or context when useful.

goals.title: Compare Linear Relationships
goals.description: Compare linear relationships using slope, starting value, outputs, and context.
i_can_statements: Compare slopes or rates.
Compare starting values or intercepts.
Use different representations to support a comparison.
Explain which relationship better fits the question being asked.

goals.title: Linear Models
goals.description: Build or use a linear model and judge whether it is useful.
i_can_statements: Use a line of fit with data.
Interpret slope and intercept in a data context.
Make a prediction within a reasonable range.
Explain when a linear model has limits.

goals.title: Solve Systems
goals.description: Solve systems by graphing, substitution, or elimination and choose a useful method.
i_can_statements: Find a system solution from a graph.
Solve a system by substitution.
Solve a system by elimination.
Identify one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.

goals.title: Systems from Situations
goals.description: Use two equations to model two constraints and interpret the solution.
i_can_statements: Define variables clearly.
Write two equations for two different constraints.
Solve the system.
Interpret both coordinates of the solution.

goals.title: Graph Linear Inequalities
goals.description: Graph a linear inequality using a boundary line and a correct solution region.
i_can_statements: Graph the boundary line.
Use a solid or dashed line correctly.
Use a test point to choose the shaded region.
Explain whether boundary points are included.

goals.title: Systems of Inequalities
goals.description: Graph more than one inequality and use the overlap to represent possible solutions.
i_can_statements: Write inequalities from constraints.
Graph the inequalities on the same plane.
Identify the feasible region.
Test whether a point satisfies all constraints.

goals.title: Recognize Function Families
goals.description: Identify common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
i_can_statements: Use differences, second differences, ratios, shape, or equation structure as evidence.
Use key features such as intercepts, vertex, symmetry, asymptotes, domain, and range when they help identify or describe a family.
Compare more than one piece of evidence before choosing a family.

goals.title: Transform Functions
goals.description: Represent translations, stretches, compressions, and reflections across function families.
i_can_statements: Move key points when a function is translated.
Recognize stretches, compressions, and reflections.
Connect equation changes to graph changes.
Describe changes in key features, including range when useful.

goals.title: Polynomial Operations and Exponents
goals.description: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials using structure, like terms, distribution, and exponent laws.
i_can_statements: Combine like polynomial terms.
Distribute signs and factors correctly.
Use product, quotient, power-of-a-power, and zero-exponent rules when they appear in polynomial work.
Check whether two polynomial forms are equivalent.

goals.title: Quadratic Structure and Graphs
goals.description: Use polynomial and quadratic structure to identify features such as zeros, vertex, symmetry, and direction of opening.
i_can_statements: Connect factors to zeros and x-intercepts.
Connect vertex form to the vertex and axis of symmetry.
Use standard form to identify useful information.
Choose the form that best shows the feature needed.

goals.title: Greatest Common Factor
goals.description: Factor polynomial expressions using a greatest common factor and check the result.
i_can_statements: Find the greatest common numerical factor.
Find common variable factors.
Factor the GCF from every term.
Multiply back to check.

goals.title: Factor Trinomials and Special Patterns
goals.description: Factor quadratic trinomials and common special patterns.
i_can_statements: Use product-sum reasoning to factor trinomials.
Use diamond problems to organize factor pairs.
Recognize difference of squares.
Recognize perfect-square trinomials.

goals.title: Factors, Zeros, and Graphs
goals.description: Use factored form to find and interpret zeros of a quadratic function.
i_can_statements: Find zeros from factored form.
Connect zeros to x-intercepts.
Write factored form from known zeros when enough information is given.
Interpret zeros in a context.

goals.title: Choose a Quadratic Form
goals.description: Compare standard, vertex, and factored forms and use the most useful form.
i_can_statements: Use standard form for useful features.
Use vertex form for vertex and symmetry.
Use factored form for zeros and x-intercepts.
Explain why one form is more useful for a question.

goals.title: Solve by Factoring
goals.description: Use factoring and the zero product property to solve quadratic equations and interpret the solutions.
i_can_statements: Set the equation equal to zero when needed.
Factor the quadratic.
Use the zero product property.
Connect solutions to zeros and x-intercepts.

goals.title: Complete the Square
goals.description: Complete the square to solve a quadratic and connect the work to vertex and symmetry.
i_can_statements: Build a perfect-square trinomial.
Keep both sides of an equation balanced.
Use square roots to solve.
Simplify common radicals such as √72, recognize an irrational result, and distinguish exact from approximate answers.

goals.title: Quadratic Formula and Discriminant
goals.description: Use the quadratic formula to solve and the discriminant to predict the number of real solutions.
i_can_statements: Identify a, b, and c.
Use the quadratic formula correctly.
Use the discriminant to predict real solutions.
Give exact or approximate answers when appropriate.

goals.title: Choose a Solution Method
goals.description: Choose and explain an efficient method for solving a quadratic equation.
i_can_statements: Choose factoring when the structure makes it useful.
Choose completing the square when it is useful.
Choose the quadratic formula when it is useful.
Explain why the chosen method fits the equation.

goals.title: Quadratic Models
goals.description: Build or use quadratic models and interpret maximums, minimums, intercepts, domains, and solutions.
i_can_statements: Use a quadratic model from data, a graph, or a context.
Interpret a vertex as a maximum or minimum.
Interpret intercepts or zeros in context.
Use a meaningful domain and reject impossible solutions.

goals.title: Recognize Exponential Change
goals.description: Identify exponential growth and decay using constant ratios, repeated multiplication, graphs, equations, tables, and contexts.
i_can_statements: Tell the difference between additive and multiplicative change.
Find and use a constant ratio.
Identify growth and decay.
Use graphs, tables, equations, or contexts as evidence.

goals.title: Write and Use Exponential Functions
goals.description: Write, evaluate, graph, and interpret exponential functions using initial value, growth/decay factor, function notation, and key features.
i_can_statements: Write an exponential function from a table, graph, or context.
Evaluate an exponential function.
Interpret the initial value and growth or decay factor.
Describe important graph features, including domain and range when useful.

goals.title: Compare Function Families
goals.description: Compare linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using differences, second differences, ratios, equations, graphs, and contexts.
i_can_statements: Use first differences for linear patterns.
Use second differences for quadratic patterns.
Use ratios for exponential patterns.
Support a function-family comparison with evidence.

goals.title: Exponential Models
goals.description: Build and analyze exponential models from real-world data, make predictions, and judge model limits.
i_can_statements: Identify or estimate an initial value and multiplicative factor.
Make a prediction from an exponential model.
Interpret model values in context.
Explain when the model may stop being useful.

goals.title: Choose a Model
goals.description: Select an appropriate linear, quadratic, or exponential model using evidence from patterns, features, representations, and context.
i_can_statements: Use differences and ratios correctly.
Use graph and equation features as evidence.
Connect the model choice to the situation.
Change the model choice when new evidence does not fit.

goals.title: Transform Across Function Families
goals.description: Analyze transformations across function families and connect parameter changes to graphs, tables, key points, and features.
i_can_statements: Use parent functions as a reference.
Track translations, reflections, stretches, and compressions.
Describe how key points and features change.
Use domain and range when they help describe the change.

goals.title: Absolute Value and Piecewise Functions
goals.description: Analyze and model absolute value and piecewise relationships using equations, graphs, intervals, domain, range, and context.
i_can_statements: Interpret the vertex and rates of an absolute-value graph.
Use interval conditions in a piecewise rule.
Determine meaningful domain and range.
Connect a rule to a graph or context.

goals.title: Modeling with Data
goals.description: Create and evaluate mathematical models from real-world data, state assumptions, make predictions, and critique model limits.
i_can_statements: Choose a model family from evidence.
State assumptions and constraints.
Make a prediction within a meaningful domain.
Explain why a model may stop being useful.

goals.title: Function Synthesis
goals.description: Synthesize equations, graphs, tables, function notation, and contexts to solve complex problems.
i_can_statements: Move among representations.
Choose a representation based on the information needed.
Check that representations describe the same relationship.
Use mathematical evidence to support a conclusion.
